samples.summary: The new `command:` attribution wiring for the five orchestrator-backed commands is untested end to end
samples.evidence: `docs.ts`, `notes.ts`, `slides.ts` and `files.ts` now pass `command: commandPath(this)` into `runDocsImport` / `runNotesImport` / `runSlidesImport` / `runFilesUpload` / `runFilesDownload`. Every test that drives those orchestrators calls them directly with hand-built args and never sets `command` (e.g. `packages/cli/test/upstream-error.test.ts:691` `runDocsImport({ file: 'a.docx', replace: 'doc-1', yes: true }, …)`, and `docs-import.test.ts`, `notes-import.test.ts`, `slides-import.test.ts`). `errorEnvelope`/`upstreamErrorJson` are tested with a `command` string passed in by the test itself. So if the `command: commandPath(this)` argument were dropped from any of those five call sites, every suite stays green and those commands silently emit unattributed envelopes — the exact behaviour this change adds. The equivalent wiring for the throwing commands IS covered (output.test.ts asserts `docs.get` / `sheets.cells.get`), which makes the gap for the orchestrator commands the untested half.

samples.summary: 'sets SameSite=Lax with secure=false outside production' asserts nothing if no cookie is issued — the loop can be empty
samples.evidence: The production sibling pins `expect(res.cookie).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2)` before iterating, but the development case (line 556-568) goes straight to `for (const [name, , options] of (res.cookie as jest.Mock).mock.calls)`. If `controller.refresh` stopped setting cookies on the non-production path (e.g. the refresh cookie name drifted so `req.cookies[refreshCookieName()]` missed and the JSON/throw branch ran instead — the very naming behaviour this diff introduces), `mock.calls` would be empty, the loop body would never execute, and the test would still pass while asserting nothing about `secure:false` or the bare cookie names. Same shape in 'never sets SameSite=None' (line 576-582), which also iterates without any count assertion.

samples.summary: `expect(options).not.toHaveProperty('domain')` cannot fail — it is presented as evidence the `__Host-` prefix is legal
samples.evidence: `baseCookieOptions()` in auth.controller.ts returns a literal with `httpOnly`, `secure`, `sameSite`, `path` only; `domain` is never a key on any code path, so this assertion holds regardless of the behaviour under test. It reads as the check that the cookie is `__Host-`-compatible, but the only way it could fail is a source change that deliberately adds a `domain` key, which nothing in the change moves toward.

samples.summary: The confirm-token binding is tested for `port` and `challenge` but not for `nonce`, and the documented length-prefix framing has no test
samples.evidence: `cliConfirmToken` signs `port`, `nonce` and `challenge` (middleware line 97-107) and its doc comment claims each part is length-prefixed 'so no combination of values can be re-cut into a different one that signs the same'. The spec covers replay against another port (line 161) and another challenge (line 174) only; dropping `nonce` from the `parts` array, or removing the `${part.length}:` framing, would leave the whole suite green. A nonce-replay case and one collision case (two parameter sets that would sign identically without framing) are what pin those claims.

samples.summary: `announceLoginUrl`: the owner-only file mode, the TTY branch and the write-failure fallback are untested
samples.evidence: The new helper's security claim is that the login URL lands in a file 'readable only by you' (`writeFileSync(file, …, { mode: 0o600 })` preceded by an `rmSync` so an existing permissive file cannot survive). `packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts` asserts only the path is announced and the content matches (`readFileSync(urlPath,'utf-8')`), never `statSync(urlPath).mode`; a grep for `0o600` in packages/cli finds only `test/session.test.ts:75` (the session file, a different writer). Neither the `process.stderr.isTTY` branch (prints the URL inline) nor the `catch` branch (the 'was not printed' message) has any test — stderr is never a TTY under vitest.

samples.summary: Nothing tests that the pino `req` serializer actually routes `req.url` through `logSafeUrl`
samples.evidence: `log-safe-url.spec.ts` exercises the helper in isolation only. Grepping the backend for `logSafeUrl` finds it in `log-safe-url.ts`, its spec and `app.module.ts` alone — there is no app.module/logging test. Reverting the one-line wiring (`url: logSafeUrl(req.url)` back to `url: req.url`) restores the credential leak the whole file exists to close while every test stays green.

samples.summary: The new env-isolation beforeEach clears `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL` but not `COOKIE_SECURE`, which now takes precedence
samples.evidence: `isSecureCookie()` (oauth-state.ts:229) reads `COOKIE_SECURE` *before* `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL` and `NODE_ENV`. The three new/updated describes in this file (lines 495, 603, 778) delete only `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL`, so a `COOKIE_SECURE` in the ambient environment (or leaked by another module in the same worker) still decides `expect(options).toMatchObject({ secure: true })` and the `__Host-` name assertions — the exact environment-dependence the added comment says it is removing. The sibling suite `github-auth.guard.spec.ts:95` does delete it, showing the intended pattern.

samples.summary: `expect(CALLBACK_TIMEOUT_MS).toBe(5 * 60 * 1000)` restates a constant and does not pin the 'two ends agree' claim
samples.evidence: The comment says "The server's budget: `STATE_COOKIE_MAX_AGE_MS` and the `CliAuthStore` state entry both expire at five minutes. The two ends must agree," but the assertion compares the CLI constant to a hard-coded literal; nothing reads the backend value, so a change to `CLI_STATE_COOKIE_MAX_AGE_MS` in `packages/backend/src/auth/oauth-state.ts:136` leaves this green. The surrounding fake-timer assertions do carry real behavioural weight, so this is a redundant line rather than the whole test being vacuous.

samples.summary: The 'warns once' test only demonstrates per-instance dedup, not the documented once-per-process behaviour
samples.evidence: `warnedInsecureOrigin` is an instance field (github-auth.guard.ts:195) documented as 'One line per process, not one per login'. The test builds one guard and calls `canActivate` twice, so it proves per-instance dedup; every other case in the file constructs a fresh `GitHubAuthGuard` per `activate()`, which would each warn again. Nothing asserts the guard is a singleton, so a scope change (REQUEST-scoped guard) would restore the log spam with the suite green.

finding.summary: The new `command:` attribution wiring for the five orchestrator-backed commands is untested end to end
finding.evidence: `docs.ts`, `notes.ts`, `slides.ts` and `files.ts` now pass `command: commandPath(this)` into `runDocsImport` / `runNotesImport` / `runSlidesImport` / `runFilesUpload` / `runFilesDownload`. Every test that drives those orchestrators calls them directly with hand-built args and never sets `command` (e.g. `packages/cli/test/upstream-error.test.ts:691` `runDocsImport({ file: 'a.docx', replace: 'doc-1', yes: true }, …)`, and `docs-import.test.ts`, `notes-import.test.ts`, `slides-import.test.ts`). `errorEnvelope`/`upstreamErrorJson` are tested with a `command` string passed in by the test itself. So if the `command: commandPath(this)` argument were dropped from any of those five call sites, every suite stays green and those commands silently emit unattributed envelopes — the exact behaviour this change adds. The equivalent wiring for the throwing commands IS covered (output.test.ts asserts `docs.get` / `sheets.cells.get`), which makes the gap for the orchestrator commands the untested half.

verdict.reason: The `command: commandPath(this)` wiring is real at all five orchestrator call sites (files.ts:46 upload, files.ts:76 download, docs.ts:356, notes.ts:249, slides.ts:249), and the orchestrators stamp it into their envelopes (files/upload.ts:152/166/177/221/229). No test exercises that wiring. The orchestrator suites call runDocsImport/runNotesImport/runSlidesImport/runFilesUpload/runFilesDownload directly with hand-built args that omit `command` (upstream-error.test.ts:685-870) and assert envelopes with no `command` key (:877, :886), so they pass with or without the argument. The commander-driven attribution suite (upstream-error.test.ts:267-341) asserts `command` for 33 argv cases but contains no `docs/notes/slides import`, `files upload`, or `files download` case; command-exit-codes.test.ts drives only content/export/get/list and never asserts `command`; files-format.test.ts drives real `files` subcommands but only rename/delete/list/get for INVALID_FORMAT. output.test.ts:355-472 tests errorEnvelope/upstreamErrorJson with a `command` string supplied by the test itself, covering the helper rather than the call sites. Repo-wide grep for error.command/command": outside node_modules finds no other test, and the backend CLI-roundtrip e2e specs assert no envelope `command`. Removing the argument from any of the five sites keeps every suite green, so the added behavior ships with no meaningful test — a major missing-test gap under the test-adequacy rubric.

finding.summary: 'sets SameSite=Lax with secure=false outside production' asserts nothing if no cookie is issued — the loop can be empty
finding.evidence: The production sibling pins `expect(res.cookie).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2)` before iterating, but the development case (line 556-568) goes straight to `for (const [name, , options] of (res.cookie as jest.Mock).mock.calls)`. If `controller.refresh` stopped setting cookies on the non-production path (e.g. the refresh cookie name drifted so `req.cookies[refreshCookieName()]` missed and the JSON/throw branch ran instead — the very naming behaviour this diff introduces), `mock.calls` would be empty, the loop body would never execute, and the test would still pass while asserting nothing about `secure:false` or the bare cookie names. Same shape in 'never sets SameSite=None' (line 576-582), which also iterates without any count assertion.

verdict.reason: The missing count assertion at auth.controller.spec.ts:556-568 is real textually, but the claimed vacuity is unreachable. issueCookies() (spec:513-534) keys the request with refreshCookieName() itself and never sets req.body, so fromBody is always false (controller:271-272) and the res.json branch (controller:292-297) cannot run; if the cookie lookup missed, controller:274-277 throws UnauthorizedException, the awaited issueCookies() rejects and the test FAILS rather than passing empty. With the mocks at spec:516-527 execution provably reaches setAuthCookies (controller:299), which calls res.cookie twice (controller:368,376), so the loop always runs 2 iterations and genuinely asserts the bare names and secure:false. The 'never sets SameSite=None' loop (spec:570-584) also consumes clearCookie calls, and clearAuthCookies (controller:349-361) unconditionally emits 4 names x 2 secure flags, so it is non-empty by construction. What is left is a hardening nit, not a vacuous test under the test-adequacy rubric.
